description: A composite group of two images that make one argument about Cr effects in Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr near-rapidly solidified strips. The top image is a rendered data table of tensile results for as-cast and annealed (550 °C, 5 h) 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr strips: as-cast YS 724±16, 617±4, 652±5 and 740±8 MPa, UTS 924±24, 896±28, 953±9 and 979±22 MPa, TE 40.8±8, 33.2±7, 31.6±1 and 20.3±5 %; annealed YS 882±6, 768±9, 751±2 and 805±11 MPa, UTS 934±4, 915±23, 965±2 and 994±21 MPa, TE 30.1±2, 37.4±5, 44.3±3 and 22.8±4 %; increment of YS after annealing +158, +151, +101, +65 MPa and increment of TE −10.7, +4.2, +12.7, +2.5 %. The lower image is a six-panel TEM montage of austenite: (a) BF of 0Cr with "Dislocation" arrows and an SADP inset indexed [001]γ+[001]κ with κ-carbide superlattice spots; (b) BF of 3Cr and (c) BF of 6Cr, both with heavy "Dislocation" content and weak superlattice, (c) inset indexed [001]γ; (d) BF of 9Cr, inset [111]γ; (e) DF of 0Cr using (010)κ showing κ-carbides only at the austenite/ferrite boundary; (f) BF of 9Cr with granular/banded Cr23C6 at grain boundaries, inset [011]Cr23C6. Scale bars are 500 nm except (e), 200 nm.

observations.observation: The table reports that as-cast yield strength is non-monotonic with Cr: 724±16 MPa (0Cr), 617±4 MPa (3Cr), 652±5 MPa (6Cr) and 740±8 MPa (9Cr), i.e. it falls at 3Cr and then rises above the Cr-free value at 9Cr.
As-cast total elongation decreases monotonically with Cr content: 40.8±8 % (0Cr), 33.2±7 % (3Cr), 31.6±1 % (6Cr) and 20.3±5 % (9Cr).
Annealing at 550 °C for 5 h raises yield strength in every strip, but the increment shrinks with Cr: +158 MPa (0Cr), +151 MPa (3Cr), +101 MPa (6Cr) and +65 MPa (9Cr).

The increment of total elongation after annealing is negative for 0Cr (−10.7 %) and positive for the Cr-containing strips (+4.2 % 3Cr, +12.7 % 6Cr, +2.5 % 9Cr), with 6Cr annealed showing the highest TE of the whole table (44.3±3 %).
As-cast UTS rises along the Cr series from 924±24 MPa (0Cr) through 896±28 MPa (3Cr) and 953±9 MPa (6Cr) to 979±22 MPa (9Cr), and is further increased by annealing in every strip.
All TEM micrographs (a)–(d) and (f) carry a 500 nm scale bar, while the dark-field image (e) carries a 200 nm scale bar.

The bright-field images of 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr all contain yellow arrows and the printed word 'Dislocation', and the corresponding SADP insets are indexed [001]γ+[001]κ for (a) and (b), [001]γ for (c) and [111]γ for (d).

Panel (e) is a dark-field image of the 0Cr strip formed with (010)κ, and the only bright κ-carbide contrast visible is located at a boundary, consistent with carbides at the austenite/ferrite phase boundary.
Panel (f) shows grain-boundary carbides in the 9Cr strip with an inset SADP indexed [011]Cr23C6 and labelled reflections (822), (911), (000) and (1̄11).

The caption states (a) is a BF image of the 0Cr strip with its corresponding SADP, (b) of 3Cr, (c) of 6Cr, (d) of 9Cr, (e) a DF image of 0Cr using (010), and (f) a BF image of 9Cr containing Cr23C6 with its SADP.
The citing text states that dislocation density in austenite increases with Cr addition and that 9Cr has a still high but slightly lower dislocation density than 6Cr.
The citing text states that the κ-carbide superlattice is clear in the 0Cr austenite pattern, very weak in 3Cr and 6Cr and absent in 9Cr, so Cr suppresses κ-carbide precipitation.

The citing text states that the Cr23C6 carbides in the 9Cr strip have a cubic structure with lattice constant 1.054 nm and granular or banded shapes about 100 nm wide, which are visible in the pixels but whose dimensions and lattice constant the image itself does not confirm.

Taken together, the group links the dislocation/carbide microstructure of the as-cast strips (TEM panels) to the tensile property changes (table), including why Cr addition lowers as-cast elongation while raising yield strength at 9Cr.

subfigures.description: Table of tensile values for as-cast and annealed (550 °C, 5 h) 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr, 9Cr strips, with columns YS(MPa), UTS(MPa), TE(%) for each condition plus increment of YS (MPa) and increment of TE (%) after annealing; every cell is legible.

Bright-field TEM image of austenite in the 0Cr strip with a 500 nm scale bar, yellow arrows and the printed label 'Dislocation'; inset SADP indexed [001]γ+[001]κ with labelled reflections (220), (020), (200), (000), (010), (100), (110) plus weak inner superlattice spots.

BF TEM image of the 3Cr strip (500 nm scale bar) showing a dense tangled dislocation network labelled 'Dislocation', with yellow arrows; inset SADP indexed [001]γ+[001]κ labelled (220), (020), (200), (000), (010) with an arrow marking a faint ring-like extra reflection.

BF TEM image of the 6Cr strip (500 nm scale bar) with heavy dislocation content labelled 'Dislocation' and yellow arrows; inset SADP indexed [001]γ with labelled (110), (010), (100), (000) reflections.

BF TEM image of the 9Cr strip (500 nm scale bar) with dislocations marked by yellow arrows and the label 'Dislocation'; inset SADP indexed [111]γ with labelled (101), (000), (1̄10), (011) reflections and no visible superlattice spots.

Dark-field TEM image of the 0Cr strip recorded using (010)κ, 200 nm scale bar, in which bright κ-carbide particles are visible only along the austenite/ferrite phase boundary; printed labels 'κ-carbides' and '(010)κ'.

BF TEM image of the 9Cr strip (500 nm scale bar) with a yellow arrow and printed label 'Cr23C6' pointing to grain-boundary carbides; inset SADP indexed [011]Cr23C6 with labelled (822), (911), (000), (1̄11) reflections.

unreadable_items: panel (b) inset SADP: the weak extra reflection marked by the arrow is only faintly legible, its superlattice origin cannot be confirmed from pixels alone
panel (a) inset SADP: the inner superlattice spots are small and their indices are not individually labelled
panels (e) and (f): fine microstructural detail (individual κ-carbide size, carbide width ~100 nm claimed in text) cannot be measured from the supplied resolution
